2026-11-06.title: Friday of the Thirty-first Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I rejoiced when I heard them say: let us go to the house of the Lord
2026-11-06.verse: And his master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than are the children of light.
theo: The parable of the dishonest manager surprises every reader. Jesus does not praise his dishonesty; he praises his shrewdness. Facing dismissal, the manager acts quickly and decisively to secure his future. Jesus' point is a challenge: worldly people put great energy into worldly goals; why are the children of light so slow and careless about eternal ones?

Paul gives the reason for urgency: “our citizenship is in heaven, and it is from there that we are expecting a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ”. Some live as “enemies of the cross of Christ”, with their minds set on earthly things. Christians are not careless about this world, but they live in it as citizens of another, and they manage everything they have as stewards who will give an account.
outline: Ask: how much energy do you give your career or exams, and how much to your soul?
Point 2 · Be shrewd for the Kingdom
Use time and money wisely for eternity.
Our true home shapes how we live here.
live: Give fifteen minutes today to planning your spiritual life as carefully as your work.
Honour the Sacred Heart: go to Confession or spend time before the Blessed Sacrament.
2026-11-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, you have made me a steward of your gifts. Make me wise and quick for your Kingdom, faithful in managing what I have, and always mindful that my citizenship is in heaven. Amen.

quick: We are stewards who will give an account.
Be as shrewd for heaven as the world is for money.
2026-11-06.action: Spend fifteen minutes planning your spiritual life.
2026-11-06.question: Where am I careless about eternal things?

homily: Dear friends, today's parable surprises everyone. A dishonest manager is about to lose his job, so he quickly reduces the debts of his master's debtors to win friends for the future. And the master praises him (Luke 16:8). Jesus does not praise his dishonesty; he praises his shrewdness.

The point is a challenge. People of this world put great energy into their worldly plans: careers, houses, investments. Why are the children of light so slow and careless about eternal things? If we planned our souls the way we plan our savings, how different our lives would be.

Paul gives the reason for urgency: our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we expect a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body (Philippians 3:20–21). We are citizens of another country, living here for a while.

This is the first Friday of the month, a day to honour the Heart of Jesus. Let us be shrewd for the Kingdom: one clear spiritual goal for this November, written down and kept where we can see it. Amen.
kids: Children, we plan our games and our holidays. Let us also plan to be close to Jesus: one prayer, one good deed, every day!

intro: We will give an account; so let us be shrewd for eternity, as citizens of heaven.

sub: The manager's time ran out suddenly.
q: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every secret thing, whether good or evil.
So he summoned him and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give me an accounting of your management, because you cannot be my manager any longer.’
points.apply: Examine your conscience tonight as a steward.

sub: The world plans carefully for its goals.
The children of light must plan for theirs.
q: Go to the ant, you lazybones; consider its ways, and be wise.
And his master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the children of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than are the children of light.
points.apply: Set one concrete spiritual goal for this month.

sub: Some are enemies of the cross.
We await a Saviour from heaven.
q: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD!”
For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
points.apply: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday.

concl: Live today as citizens of heaven.
2026-11-06.resolve: Write one spiritual goal for November and keep it where you see it.
